items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: I remember we would finish a tour and it would be, we’d go in the studio and it would be ... Dizzy and Roy ... and myself ... he’d say, “What are you guys going to play?”

ctx.x: Norman Granz was a pretty important figure in jazz during those years. Was he a pretty upright guy to work for?

Oh yeah. You know he did a lot of brilliant things. First of all he put jazz into the concert hall. He took it out of the dance hall and put it in the concert hall. He took it out of the night club and put it in the concert hall. He gave people the very best musicians, I mean he got the top people, he always had top people playing for him, and he paid top salaries. I mean he was a tough guy. I remember we would finish a tour and it would be, we’d go in the studio and it would be Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, Ben…

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: He said, 'You know that show, when I hired you guys, Teddy and Al Hall...' Specs stayed on, because he got... He did get a break, because he got with this other cat, who was on The Ed Sullivan Show, Ray Brown. And Specs, Roy Eldridge, Al Hall, Teddy Wilson and Al Casey.

ctx.x: And you said they had pickets outside?

Yeah. I met Paul Baron in Rome. He was conducting a symphony in Rome, you know. And he said, "Well, they finally got me out of the country." This is going back a little bit, too. I said, "Yeah?" He said, "You know that show, when I hired you guys, Teddy and Al Hall..." Specs stayed on, because he got... He did get a break, because he got with this other cat, who was on The Ed Sullivan Show, Ray Brown. And Specs, Roy Eldridge, Al Hall, Teddy Wilson and Al Casey.
